title: For teams
description: Evaluate reusable agent skills with a small pilot, reviewable selections, and clear adoption boundaries.
intro: Give your team a shared starting point.
lede: Reusable playbooks for the coding agents you already use. Start with one workflow, inspect the instructions, and keep your team in control.

sections.title: Choose a practical first workflow
sections.body: Explore focused packs for building web apps, reviewing security, testing software, or automating repetitive work. A pack is a starting point: inspect its skills and requirements before adopting it.

sections.title: Run a small pilot
sections.body: Pick one task in a non-sensitive project. Read the relevant SKILL.md files, check external tools and credentials, and follow the guide for your agent. Review proposed actions and judge the result against your own acceptance criteria.

sections.title: Share a reviewable selection
sections.body: Use the catalog shortlist to compare skills and share their exact IDs with colleagues. Shared links include the catalog version and IDs only; they are not private links or snapshots of old skill content. Keep project details out of the URL.

sections.title: Make adoption repeatable
sections.body: Record the exact skill IDs and catalog version in your team workflow. With AAS Core, your agent selects the skills; validation checks the manifest and catalog, and planning produces a reviewable artifact. The Workbench inspects imported artifacts in browser memory.

sections.title: What to check before wider use
sections.body: Review each skill’s source, license, declared risk, limitations, and required services. AAS is community-maintained open source; it does not provide a service-level agreement, compliance certification, or guaranteed agent outcomes. Model providers and optional services have their own terms and costs.

title: Trust & transparency
description: Understand AAS sources, licenses, privacy, review boundaries, and security reporting.
lede: AAS is an independent, community-curated project. Inspect the source and decide whether each skill fits your environment.

sections.title: Source and review
sections.body: The GitHub repository is the canonical source. Skill details expose recorded source, requirements, and declared risk where available. Metadata and schema validation are useful checks; they do not certify security, compliance, or fitness for your project. Review the instructions and bundled files before use.

sections.title: Licenses and attribution
sections.body: Original code and tooling use MIT. Original documentation and other non-code written content use CC BY 4.0 unless a more specific upstream notice applies. Imported skills may carry additional license and attribution requirements. Check the relevant files before redistribution or commercial adoption.

sections.title: Browser data and analytics
sections.body: Saved skills and shortlists stay in this browser’s local storage. Workbench imports stay in memory. Shared links contain selected IDs and a catalog version, and anyone with the link can read them. The hosted catalog uses Vercel Web Analytics for aggregate visit statistics; AAS removes query strings and fragments from analytics URLs. The catalog also requests public aggregate skill-save counts from Supabase.

sections.title: Local tools and third parties
sections.body: Skills-only plugins are local instruction bundles and do not independently collect telemetry. AAS Core’s local catalog discovery is read-only and offline-capable. Your agent client, model provider, and any services you enable handle data under their own policies. A skill mentioning a service does not grant access or include its fees.

sections.title: Report a problem
sections.body: Use GitHub issues for reproducible bugs and Discussions for support. Send sensitive vulnerability reports through private security reporting; do not include credentials or private project information in public posts.

title: AAS Core plugin
description: A free remote MCP plugin to discover AAS skills, inspect their sources and validate agent-selected stacks.
intro: Find skills. Inspect sources. Validate your stack.
lede: AAS Core brings the public AAS skill catalog to compatible ChatGPT and Codex clients. Free remote preview, published by Niccolò Lucioli.

sections.title: From a task to a reviewable selection
sections.body: Describe the capability you need. Your agent can search the catalog, read complete skill instructions and supporting files, then choose exact skill IDs. Core checks the selected stack and compares manifests; it does not rank skills or certify their suitability.

sections.title: A read-only remote preview
sections.body: The server retrieves public catalog material and validates data supplied by your client. It cannot access your local files, install skills, run catalog scripts or deploy projects. Treat returned instructions as untrusted material and review their licenses and requirements before use.

sections.title: Availability and access
sections.body: This preview is currently private as an OpenAI plugin. Public directory installation will be available only after review. Developers can connect an MCP client to https://aas-core.aas-core-remote.workers.dev/mcp using Streamable HTTP. Sessions last up to 20 minutes and usage limits apply. The service may become unavailable when its free allowance is exhausted.

sections.title: Free, with clear boundaries
sections.body: AAS Core has no purchases, subscription or paid AI API. Your chosen AI client and optional services have their own terms and may have costs. The remote service runs in a separate Cloudflare Workers Free account, independent of the AAS website.

title: AAS Core privacy
description: How the AAS Core remote preview handles tool arguments, temporary sessions and abuse-prevention counters.
intro: Privacy for the AAS Core remote preview.
lede: Publisher: Niccolò Lucioli. Updated 29 October 2026. This notice covers the remote MCP service; local AAS bundles and the website have separate data flows.

sections.title: Data your client sends
sections.body: Your client sends MCP tool arguments to the Cloudflare-hosted service. These may include search queries, project goals, skill IDs, manifests and optional selection evidence. Do not send credentials, secrets or sensitive project information. The service cannot read your local filesystem or execute catalog scripts.

sections.title: Temporary sessions
sections.body: Arguments and selection traces remain in an isolated session’s memory and are not intentionally persisted. A session is usable for 20 minutes, can be deleted by an MCP DELETE request and can end earlier on eviction. An expiry alarm is scheduled to discard its in-memory server; infrastructure scheduling may delay cleanup.

sections.title: Abuse prevention
sections.body: The service processes the connecting IP address and stores a SHA-256 hash with usage counters until the next UTC daily boundary. Expired counters are removed on subsequent guard requests. These hashes are pseudonymous, not anonymous. Application code does not write raw IP addresses to storage.

sections.title: Service providers and the website
sections.body: Application request logging is disabled. The remote application uses no advertising, payment service or paid AI model API. Cloudflare processes connection metadata under its own policy. Your AI client processes prompts and outputs under its own policy. These informational pages on aaskills.tech use the website’s existing hosting and aggregate Vercel Web Analytics; query strings and fragments are removed before analytics events are sent. The remote application does not send tool arguments to that analytics service.

sections.title: Questions and deletion
sections.body: Use the support page for privacy questions. Do not disclose private data in public discussions. Active clients can delete their session through MCP; clearing the session does not erase records held independently by your AI client, Cloudflare or GitHub under their own policies.

title: AAS Core terms
description: Terms for the free AAS Core remote preview, its availability, acceptable use and read-only boundaries.
intro: Terms of use for the remote preview.
lede: Publisher: Niccolò Lucioli. Updated 29 October 2026. These terms apply to the AAS Core remote MCP service.

sections.title: Free experimental service
sections.body: AAS Core is a free experimental read-only catalog service. It offers no purchases or payment flows. Usage limits, short-lived sessions and infrastructure failures can make it unavailable. No availability guarantee is offered.

sections.title: Acceptable use
sections.body: Use the service only with authorization and in compliance with applicable law and platform rules. Do not abuse the endpoint, evade quotas, expose secrets or use it for harmful or unlawful activity.

sections.title: Review before use
sections.body: Returned skill text is untrusted material. Structural validation does not certify fitness, safety or compatibility. Review instructions, licenses, prerequisites and generated output before use. The service does not install skills, execute scripts or provide professional advice.

sections.title: Licenses and third parties
sections.body: Original AAS code is MIT-licensed. Written content and individual skills may carry other notices, which remain controlling. Your use of the host AI client and Cloudflare remains subject to their respective terms and policies.

sections.title: No warranty and support
sections.body: The service and its output are provided as is, without warranties. Get help through the support page. Your client and optional third-party services may have their own charges; AAS Core does not charge for this remote preview.

title: AAS Core support
description: Get help with the AAS Core remote plugin or privately report a security issue.
lede: Publisher: Niccolò Lucioli. Community support for the free remote preview.

sections.title: Ask a question or report an issue
sections.body: Use AAS GitHub Discussions for ordinary support. Include the failing tool name, a non-sensitive reproduction and the error message. Do not post credentials, private project files, session IDs or sensitive personal data.

sections.title: Report a sensitive security issue
sections.body: Use GitHub private security reporting for sensitive vulnerabilities. Do not post exploit details or private data in public discussions.

sections.title: If the service is temporarily unavailable
sections.body: The preview uses free infrastructure with bounded sessions and usage quotas. A 429 response indicates a usage limit; wait before trying again. A missing or expired session requires a new MCP initialization. An exhausted daily allowance can keep the remote service unavailable until reset, independently of the AAS website.

title: Sponsors & Supporters
description: Meet the open-source programs supporting Agentic Awesome Skills: Codex, Vercel, Snyk, Atlas Cloud, and BrowserStack.
lede: The organizations helping keep Agentic Awesome Skills free, open, and independently maintained.

sections.title: Financial Sponsors
sections.body: Financial contributions support ongoing maintenance, skill reviews, and release work. Help keep Agentic Awesome Skills free and independently maintained.

sections.title: Infrastructure & Tooling Supporters
sections.body: Tools, platform access, and credits provided through open-source programs.

sections.title: Codex for Open Source
sections.body: OpenAI’s program supports open-source maintainers with access to Codex for coding, review, and maintenance work. Thank you for supporting AAS.

sections.title: Vercel Open Source Program
sections.body: Vercel supports open-source projects with platform credits and resources for building on the web. AAS is part of the 2026 program.

sections.title: Snyk for Open Source
sections.body: Snyk provides security tooling for open-source projects. Its support helps AAS maintainers examine code and dependencies for vulnerabilities.

sections.title: Atlas Cloud Open Source Program
sections.body: Atlas Cloud supports AAS with AI compute and model credits, including the image and video generation workflows documented in the atlas-cloud-media skill.

sections.title: BrowserStack Open Source Program
sections.body: BrowserStack supports open-source projects with access to real browsers and devices. This project is tested with BrowserStack.
